title: Youth Services Specialist
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Youth Services Specialist supports IRC's Refugee School Impact (RSI) program, helping ORR-eligible refugee students (ages 6-18) and their parents or guardians’ access and succeed in the U.S. education system. The Specialist helps families enroll their children in school, leads student and parent orientations, provides after-school tutoring and academic support during the school year, and runs a summer academic program. The Specialist also checks in regularly with students to track academic progress and coordinates with school staff, community partners, and the Education & Youth Services Manager to keep services aligned with program goals.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist newly arrived ORR-eligible families with school enrollment for children ages 6–18, including interpretation support as needed.
- Provide school orientation to enrolled students and lead Extended School Orientation workshops for parents and guardians, covering topics such as school choice, transportation, attendance, and how to support their child's education.
- Coordinate with Jefferson County Public Schools (JCPS) Office of Multilingual Learners and other school staff to identify enrollment issues early and keep teachers informed of students' academic progress.
- Support families choosing private schools, homeschools, or districts outside JCPS, including newly arrived refugee families served through the Program of Initial Resettlement.
- Deliver the after-school program twice a week during the school year, providing tutoring in reading and writing and other academic support, with the help of interns or volunteers.
- Conduct regular one-on-one check-ins with students at school to track grades, homework completion, and attendance, and coordinate with teachers to address concerns early.
- Refer students and families to IRC programs or other community resources when needs arise outside of school.
- Plan and lead the summer academic program, including academic reinforcement, enrichment activities, field trips, and transportation to and from students' homes.
- Maintain accurate and timely documentation of services, referrals, and orientations in ClientTrack.
- Assist in the recruitment, training, and supervision of interns or other youth program staff.
- Attend regular meetings with the Education & Youth Services Manager to discuss programming and any concerns.
- Support case closures, transition planning, and other closeout activities as the program year winds down.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work, education, or a related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Experience working with refugee, immigrant, or other multicultural youth and families, preferably in a school, resettlement, or case management setting.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Familiarity with the U.S. education system, or willingness to learn local school district processes and requirements, is preferred. Experience with a client database system (such as ClientTrack) is a plus.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle, with the ability to transport clients as needed.
- Required to drive clients for school enrollment, summer programs, and after school.
- First Aid and CPR certification preferred (or willingness to obtain before the start of the program).

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional domestic (non-local) travel required; up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $21-$23/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: ESOL Instructor
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:**

The ESOL Instructor is responsible for providing integrated English language instruction for non-native English speakers. The instructor must be able to successfully develop and tailor curriculum and materials to the needs of students enrolled into the program including the support of student recruitment, registration, attendance tracking, retention, progress, and assessment.

This is a part-time, approx. 7 hours per week, reporting to the Adult Education Specialist. Classes and registrations are held at the IRC Richmond office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Deliver integrated ESOL instruction
    - Plan and prepare curricula and lesson plans for mixed-level classes to meet the English language learning needs of students. Integrated ESOL combines English language lessons with job skills and workforce preparation, digital literacy skills, civics, and other life skills.
    - Tune lesson activities to meet student needs across a range of English proficiency levels, from the most basic through intermediate and advanced levels of speaking, comprehension, reading, and writing.
    - Utilize and oversee community volunteers as classroom assistants, managing the delivery of lesson plan activities through those assistants in breakout groups.
    - Document student progress with goal setting and conference notes and assist in recruitment and retention activities.
- Orient and conference with current and potential students, assisting students in completing necessary intake and enrollment forms, both virtually, using phone and web-based platforms, and in-person.
- Administer English language assessments to measure and track student progress and gains.
- Assist with record-keeping and data entry to support program administration and compliance with programmatic requirements. Document student progress by keeping accurate and timely attendance records, case notes, assessment data, program participant surveys, and observations of student progress.
- Maintain a positive learning environment. Facilitate student learning activities that build cultural and community knowledge and encourage collaboration and positive peer support.
- Maintain open and effective communication with adult education team members. Report regularly on program goals, client attendance, learning activities, student progress and any problems or concerns with clients or program.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (4-year) preferred.
- Completion of a certificate program in Adult Education, TEFL, TESL, and/or TESOL is preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant teaching experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with immigrants or refugees preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies**

- Strong desire to support vulnerable individuals and families and enthusiasm for working in a multi-cultural setting.
- Enthusiasm for adult education and language learning.
- An interest in immigrant and refugee and asylee issues and the resettlement process.
- Strong communication abilities, including the ability to lead classes and oversee community volunteers and adult learners.
- Detail oriented and comfortable working with online databases.
- Comfortable working in a cross-cultural environment, in-person, online, and over the phone, with adult learners, sometimes with little or no English proficiency.
- Ability to take initiative, work independently on projects, and follow through on critical tasks.
- Ability to work in a collaborative environment, co-teaching and facilitating learning through others.
- Strong time management skills and comfortability with computer and web-based office and communication platforms.
- Fluent in spoken and written English. Bi-lingual abilities in a language spoken by an IRC client group are desired.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $22.75 - $24.20/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of Programme
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Head of Programme.

Danish Refugee Council is a leading protection agency pursuing our mandate to protect and promote durable solutions to displacement-affected populations based on humanitarian principles. In East Africa and the Great Lakes, DRC has operational presence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

In the DR Congo, DRC has been involved in humanitarian aid since 2009. Initially working in Province Orientale, DRC gradually extended its reach to North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The sectors of intervention for DRC in the country are provision of Emergency Response, Protection (including GBV and child protection), Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH. DRC is currently responding to the Ebola outbreak as this is unfolding in Ituri province where DRC has a longstanding presence.

**About the job**

Provide strategic direction, leadership and oversight of DRC’s country programme, ensuring coherent strategy, high programme quality, effective departmental management and sustainable funding. Lead country-level programme development and support accountable implementation through Area Managers and Project Managers. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the HoP oversees a multi-sector portfolio spanning emergency response, early recovery and resilience in eastern DR Congo, including consortia led by DRC, and works closely with the Head of Support Services and the Head of Safety to balance programme excellence, cost efficiency and safety.

**Main Responsibilities**

*Programme Strategy & Development*

- Lead and periodically review the Country Programme Plan, Theory of Change and sector/geographic priorities; translate strategy into clear departmental workplans.
- Coordinate an integrated, multi-sector approach across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; ensure the centrality of protection, safe programming, access and adherence to humanitarian principles; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
- Promote cash and market-based programming (including multi-purpose and emergency cash) and link emergency response with early recovery and durable solutions.
- Drive innovative programme design with the SMT, in line with DRC global and regional strategies.

*Programme Coordination*

- Lead the Programme Department; clarify reporting lines, roles, delegation, staffing and cost structure with the Head of Support Services.
- In collaboration with the Area Manager, maintain consolidated priorities, deliverables and follow-up
- Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
- Oversee portfolio quality and delivery; work with Area Managers on operational feasibility, project start-up/closure and timely escalation of implementation risks.
- Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
- Coordinate programme approaches across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
- Maintain programme risks and mitigation actions in the Country Office Risk Register; analyze options and take timely decisions within delegatedauthority.
- Provide concise, decision-oriented updates to SMT and coordinate priorities with Area Offices, Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Safety, Regional Hub and HQ.
- Ensure effective and transparent planning and use of financial resources (budget follow-up, burn rates) in compliance with DRC and donor rules; keep programme staff updated on donor regulations.

*Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)*

- Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
- Ensure monitoring systems produce quality evidence that is used for programme adjustment and accountability to affect populations; document and share lessons learned and good practices internally and externally.

*Fundraising, Proposal Development & Reporting*

- Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
- Oversee timely, quality concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports with Grants, Finance and field teams, in line with DRC and donor requirements.

*Donor Liaison, Partnerships & Representation*

- Represent DRC with donors, consortia, coordination bodies, authorities and local partners; advance localization and coherent programme positioning; ensure effective governance of DRC-led consortia.
- Deputize for the Country Director when delegated.

*Advocacy & Communication*

- With the CD and the Advocacy & Communications function, develop evidence-based advocacy messages grounded in programme data, promoting the protection and rights of displaced and conflict-affected populations.
- Support the development and review of external communication materials (case studies, success stories, donor visibility).

*People management*

- Providing leadership and direction to a team, ensuring clarity of roles, expectations, and performance standards to achieve agreed goals and objectives.
- Exercising team budget oversight and decision-making authority where assigned.
- Leading or contributing to recruitment processes for staff within their team
- Conducting and/or signing off on performance appraisals and ensuring regular, constructive feedback to support continuous improvement.
- Supporting the professional development of team members through coaching, capacity building, and development planning.
- Addressing poor performance and disciplinary issues, including handling Code of Conduct cases referred to management, in line with DRC policies and procedures.

*Technical supervision – Field Offices*

- Providing technical direction, guidance, and where mandated, instructions to ensure compliance with DRC policies, standards, and strategies.
- Supporting managers and technical staff through regular communication, capacity building, and promotion of best practices.
- Support managers with assessing the technical skills and performance of most senior technical staff in the Country/Field offices.
- Escalating and, where authorized, addressing issues of non-compliance or poor performance in line with the technical supervision mandate.
- Participating in the recruitment of most senior technical staff in Country/Field offices.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to At least 7 years in humanitarian/development programming, including at least 4 years managing staff and senior country-level programme responsibilities. Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Proven strategic planning, Theory of Change, multi-sector programme management, institutional fundraising, proposal and budget development experience.
- Master’s degree in international development, Humanitarian Affairs, Political Science, Economics, Social Sciences or related discipline.
- Strong management, delegation, prioritisation, decision-making, PCM, grants/MEAL oversight, donor compliance, partnership and communication skills; experience in complex contexts.
- Sound knowledge of displacement issues and related international standards; knowledge of the DR Congo / Great Lakes context is a strong asset.
- Proven experience of external representation with donors, authorities and clusters, and of managing programmes within consortia.
- Experience of leading change processes (scale-up/scale-down) and of working in insecure, rapidly changing environments.
- English – full professional proficiency.
- French – professional proficiency highly desirablefull professional proficiency required

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: *1 Year*

Band: *Management E*

Work location: *Bunia*

Designation of Duty Station: *Non-Accompanied*

Start date: *2nd January 2027*

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of , please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/) for more details.

title: Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL · UK NAMED COMMUNITY SPONSORSHIP PROGRAMME

**Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom**

*London area based (hybrid) · Full-time*

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

We are seeking a Senior Policy and Programme Officer, United Kingdom to join Pathways International’s powerful global team at a formative moment for the UK’s new named community sponsorship programme.

This is a broad, versatile role spanning programme and partnership delivery and policy. You will plan and deliver the projects and partnerships that build the named community sponsorship ecosystem, while also helping shape policy development and implementation and keeping the programme informed by wider migration developments. The balance between policy and delivery will flex with the needs of the programme and the shape of the UK team.

Reporting to Hannah Gregory, Global Director Knowledge and Sponsorship, and working closely with Pathways International’s UK and global teams, you will help shape and sustain the development of named community sponsorship in the UK.

**Responsibilities**

- Contributing to the development of the UK named community sponsorship policy framework, supporting the design and development of the framework post-launch, including sponsored labour and education routes, in coordination with colleagues and partners.
- Planning, delivering and coordinating projects across the UK named community sponsorship portfolio, including organising events and meetings, developing resources, materials and tools and supporting monitoring, reporting and learning.
- Building and maintaining relationships across government, civil society, local partners and funders, and communities across the UK, and connecting delivery partners to training, mentoring and resources, including via Pathways International’s global networks and UK partners.
- Supporting the multi-stakeholder working group, engaging government and other policy stakeholders (including preparing for and following up on meetings and events), and representing the programme externally.
- Building and maintaining an understanding of the national, devolved, regional and local landscape relevant to sponsorship, and drawing out its implications for the programme.
- Maintaining an overview of wider migration developments in the UK and globally, and advising on their relevance for named community sponsorship.
- Researching, analysing and drafting high-quality briefings, policy documents and other written materials for senior stakeholders.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

We are looking for a versatile person who can move comfortably between programme and partnership delivery and policy thinking, and who thrives on a varied portfolio in a fast-paced environment. You combine professionalism and maturity with the warmth and versatility to build rapport quickly across very different audiences.

- A proven understanding of one or more relevant fields, which may include forced displacement, refugee protection, community sponsorship, global migration or migration policy.
- At least eight (8) years of relevant work experience, spanning programme or project delivery and policy, research or analysis, including experience of working in or closely with government.
- Experience working with and convening NGOs, civil society and/or other delivery partners.
- A confident representative with an easy, approachable manner, who builds lasting relationships with a wide range of UK stakeholders — government, civil society and others — and brings the judgement to handle senior meetings and the readiness to get stuck into the practical details of running an event.
- Strong policy capability, able to research, analyse and draft high-quality briefings and materials for senior stakeholders with keen attention to detail.
- Excellent project-management and organisational skills, able to coordinate meetings, events and projects and to prioritise effectively across competing demands.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Able to work on a varied and constantly evolving portfolio, while consistently displaying professionalism, discretion, tact and responsibility.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field (e.g. public policy, public affairs, political science, international development). Education and work experience equivalencies will be considered.
- Comfortable preparing well-presented PowerPoint and Word documents and using AI tools, Excel, Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint.
- We particularly encourage applications from qualified candidates with lived experience of forced displacement or migration, or with close personal and cultural connections to refugee communities.

**Location**

This is a London area based hybrid-working role with the ability to travel within the UK on a regular basis as needed and access available to shared office space. Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in the UK. Maintaining such legal right to work is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

Full-time. \[One-year term (renewable), or permanent — confirm.\]

**How to apply**

Please submit a cover letter, a CV, and a short, unedited writing sample of no more than five pages (in English) through Pathways International’s BambooHR portal at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/61) by Friday, November 20th at 11:59 pm EST to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.

title: Head of Programme
body:
**What we are looking for**

Are you an accomplished humanitarian leader with the strategic vision, fundraising expertise, and leadership influence to shape refugee and humanitarian portfolio in Jordan?

This is not simply a programme management position. We are looking for a strategic leader who can identify opportunities, influence key stakeholders, strengthen localization, and secure the funding required to expand impact for refugees and vulnerable communities across Jordan.

You will be entrusted with shaping the future direction of NRC's programme portfolio while ensuring excellence in programmatic delivery, accountability, compliance, learning, and organisational growth.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking an exceptional **Head of Programme** to join its senior leadership team in Jordan. This is a pivotal Country Management Group (CMG) role, responsible for leading programme strategy, resource mobilization, grants, MEAL, partnerships, and programme quality across a complex and dynamic humanitarian environment.

As a key member of the country leadership team, you will play a central role in delivering NRC Jordan's 2026-2030 Country Strategy while driving sustainable growth through innovative programming, strategic donor engagement, and strong partnerships with national and international stakeholders.

Key responsibilities:

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight to the Programme, Grants, and MEAL functions.
- Lead the implementation of NRC Jordan's strategic objectives and ensure alignment with country priorities and annual action plans.
- Drive the development and execution of NRC Jordan's fundraising and resource mobilization strategy.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, strategic partners, consortium members, government bodies, and humanitarian actors.
- Identify emerging funding opportunities and position NRC competitively for future growth.
- Lead grant portfolio management, ensuring high-quality proposal development, compliance, reporting, and donor stewardship.
- Champion programme quality, evidence-based programming, accountability, and organisational learning.
- Strengthen partnerships with local and national actors and lead NRC's transition towards more locally led programming approaches.
- Foster collaboration between technical and operational teams to ensure effective programme delivery.
- Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technical specialists and programme support functions.

**What you will bring**

- Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences, International Relations, or a related field**.**
- Minimum 6 years of experience in a senior management position within a humanitarian or recovery context, with responsibility for programme and/or project management.
- Experience in NRC Core Competency programming (ICLA, Shelter, and Education) is an asset.
- A strong and demonstrated track record in fundraising and donor engagement, including securing significant institutional funding, developing donor relationships, identifying funding opportunities, and shaping winning resource mobilization strategies.
- Deep knowledge of humanitarian programming, programme quality standards, grants management, and MEAL systems. Experience in integrating evidence-based approaches and programme quality standards throughout the project cycle.
- Strong understanding of donor priorities, compliance requirements, and the evolving humanitarian and refugee landscape in Jordan and the region
- Proven experience building and managing partnerships with local and national actors.
- Experience leading multi-sector, consortium-based, and partnership-driven programmes.
- Outstanding stakeholder engagement, influencing, and representation skills with strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving, team-building, interpersonal and conflict-resolution capabilities.
- The ability to lead, inspire, and develop diverse teams in complex and rapidly changing environments.
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal and excellent writing skills.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDLfnFLI5MKTaemBSTg1EC-Adc-h353hZJskxlm_J4cHhM?e=zKz0i0) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman, Jordan
- Fixed term contract: 12 months, renewable based on funding, performance and the need for the position
- Travel: 30% to Area and Field Offices (NRC Operational Areas)
- Salary/benefits: Grade 11 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Jordan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/jordan)

title: Coach Support Program Internship at Yoga and Sports with Refugees - Athens
body:
## **Aim of the internship**

The CSP focuses on the personal and professional development of coaches with refugee backgrounds, with the wider goal of promoting social inclusion and support for coaches coming from diverse cultural backgrounds. The program ensures access to skill-building opportunities, certifications and leadership experience by enabling coaches to lead classes, develop their teaching methodology and expand their career pathways both within and beyond YSR.We are seeking a passionate and dedicated intern to join the CSP team in Athens. This role offers an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience in promoting an inclusive, supportive and empowering environment for our coach community.

## **Key Responsibilities**

- Foster coaches' wellbeing and sense of belonging within the YSR community, including assisting with distribution of food items and NFIs (Non-Food Items) when required
- Conduct surveys and collect feedback from coaches in coordination with the M&E team and Coach Coordinator
- Provide support on the ground by checking sports materials and equipment, identifying needs, and replacing/restocking items when necessary
- Promote coaches’ classes and ensure visibility on social media (in collaboration with the Communications Manager)
- Assist the Coach Coordinator with outreach — identifying new coaches and partners for the CSP
- Attend and support sports classes and take shifts where needed to ensure smooth implementation of activities
- Support administrative tasks (reports, updates, Canva materials, reimbursement support)
- Assist in planning and implementing events that promote community building and strengthen social inclusion

**What we offer:**

- The chance to support the growth of a dynamic organisation
- Immersion in the inner workings of a non-profit organisation
- Inclusion in an amazing community
- Participation in sport activities
- Development of analytical, writing, researching, and networking skills
- Collaboration with diverse teams from around the world
- Mentorship and professional development opportunities.
- The chance to make a meaningful impact on the community.

**What we're looking for:**

- Minimum age of 21
- Commitment of at least 3 months
- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Strong organizational and time management skills
- Independence and previous NGO experience preferred
- Passion for event organisation
- Passion for Sport and human rights
- Some experience in administrative tasks
- Eagerness to learn and take on new challenges
- Flexibility and adaptability
- Passion for diversity, equity, and inclusion.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a multicultural working environment
- Computer skills and Google tools skills

title: Communication and Advocacy Internship at Yoga and Sports with Refugees - Lesvos or Athens
body:
**Aim of the internship:**

The Communication and Advocacy Intern will contribute to raising awareness of the situation of people on the move in Greece and France, while strengthening the visibility of Yoga and Sports with Refugees (YSR), its activities, and its impact.

This internship offers a unique opportunity to combine academic learning with hands-on experience in a grassroots organization supporting displaced people, including asylum seekers and refugees. The intern will contribute to communication, advocacy, fundraising, and community-building efforts, helping amplify the voices and experiences of people on the move and highlight the role of sports in fostering inclusion, well-being, and solidarity.

**Work Tasks:**

**On the Ground Communication**

- Design flyers for events, schedules of the gym and invitations for classes
- Take pictures and videos in YSR activities such as classes, competitions, events or teamtrips
- Support fundraising campaigns by documenting activities, communicating their impact, and creating engaging content for donors and supporters.

title: Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead - MENAU
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Jordan and Lebanon.**

**CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than forty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.

With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs—improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead for MENAU is a key member of IRC’s Regional Management Team, ensuring a strategic approach to policy and advocacy engagement across the region. The role aims to influence the policies and practices of key national, regional and global decision-makers while translating the experience and expertise of IRC programmes and partners into influence at national, regional and global levels.

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead provides strategic leadership and support to country programmes, while leading on policy and, advocacy and managing in partnership IRC’s communications efforts across the region. S/he leads the development of regional policy positions and ensures that MENAU advocacy products are strategically aligned, evidence-based and meet the quality and standards expected by the organisation.

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead represents IRC on regional policy and advocacy platforms, helping to shape debate and ensuring the perspectives and priorities of country programmes and partner organizations are at the forefront of humanitarian and development decision-making. Working closely with global colleagues, s/he also ensures that regional realities shape the IRC's wider policy and advocacy positions.

Reporting to the MENAU Regional Vice President, with a management in partnership to Global Policy and Advocacy team, namely the Global Director of Program Advocacy and Engagement, Director – Policy and Advocacy and works closely with global Policy and Advocacy, while supervising and supporting regional and country level policy, advocacy and communication staff. The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead is based in Amman or Beirut with frequent travel in the region, and as needed to New York, Washington D.C., London, Brussels, Geneva and other capitals.

**SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Overall Strategy and Team Management:**

- In close coordination with the Regional Vice President, leads the development, alignment and implementation of policy and advocacy strategy for the region.
- In close coordination with the global Policy and Advocacy team, contributes to and supports the implementation of organizational strategies.
- Builds and maintains relationships with diverse MENAU organizations and individuals to develop networks and increase collective impact.
- Maintains overall accountability for regional and country-based policy, advocacy and communications team cohesion, product delivery and ensures all products meet the quality and standard set by the organization.

**2. Advocacy and Policy:**

- Works in close collaboration with country-level and global policy and advocacy colleagues, to develop and drive policy and advocacy products for in-country, regional and international policymakers, ensuring that field priorities and perspectives are integrated.
- Coordinates and supports the work of country-level policy and advocacy staff and ensures that country-focused information and materials are widely disseminated internally and externally.
- Supports the development of policy and advocacy material for national, regional and global use including talking points, briefing notes, position papers and advocacy reports.
- Supports IRC’s efforts to scale the most impactful programmatic interventions by crafting strategies to overcome political and policy barriers to their deployment nationally, regionally, while informing global debates.
- Provides policy review for organizational positions and materials related to key issues in MENAU.
- Represents IRC in regional advocacy, policy and coordination forums, as well as at key lobbying meetings in global capitals, the UN and where necessary.
- Provides analysis and produces content for executive and regional leadership and ensures the Regional Vice President is briefed on all relevant policy developments.

**3. Communications and Media:**

- Provide day-to-day management of the Deputy Director of Public Affairs and Communications, MENAU to ensure regional alignment of the regional public affairs and communications strategy.
- Support the expansion of IRC’s reach and visibility in the region, acting as an IRC spokesperson with regional and international media.
- Ensures consistent advocacy messages, calls to actions and policy asks in external communications products, including press releases, talking points, and spokesperson briefings.
- Collaborates with Deputy Director on polished and accessible external communications materials to inform key audiences and influence policy decisions.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:** Management in Partnership of the MENAU Deputy Director of Public Affairs and Communications and their team. Management in Partnership of the ECD Policy, Advocacy and Communications Lead, as well as Management in Partnership of country-level policy and advocacy staff.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:**

**Internal:** Regional Vice President; MENAU Regional Management Team; MENAU Country Directors; global policy and advocacy staff and Vice President for Global Policy and Advocacy with Management in Partnership with the Director of Program Advocacy and Engagement, global communication staff with close coordinate with the Director of Global Public Affairs and Communication; country and regional based staff as appropriate.

**External:** Regional and national advocacy fora, international and national NGOs, UN agencies, public and private donor agencies, national governments/authorities, regional and international media representatives.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- University Degree in Communications, International Affairs, Policy & Advocacy, Political Science, or any other relevant field. Master’s degree is preferable.
- At least ten years of increasingly responsible professional experience responding to complex humanitarian crises and/or post-conflict situations, with a track record of delivering change through highly impactful policy, advocacy and communications strategies
- A keen understanding of political complexities in the MENAU region is required; previous experience working in the Middle East is required
- Solid communications and media relations experience required
- Fluency in English and Arabic (written and spoken) is required, with demonstrated outstanding writing skills.
- Proven ability to persuade and influence diverse audiences
- Excellent analytical, presentation, communication and reporting skills
- Ability to navigate interpersonal and inter-departmental organizational dynamics to keep focus on goals and products
- Must be willing and able to travel regularly within the region and occasionally internationally
- Culturally sensitive, able and interested in working with a multi-ethnic team
- Arabic Speaking candidates from the Middle East region are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Advocacy Advisor Multi Country (Nairobi Based, Open for Kenyans only)
body:
**Background:**

The humanitarian situation in Somalia and Kenya in 2026 remains among the most severe and protracted, driven by conflict, economic pressures, climate shocks, disease outbreaks, mass displacement, and shrinking humanitarian funding.

Conflict and climate shocks in Somalia fuel internal displacement, placing additional pressure on already overstretched services and humanitarian systems.

NRC works in Somalia to protect the rights of displaced and vulnerable people during crisis and meet immediate humanitarian needs, prevent further displacement, and contribute to durable solutions. Access remains a significant operational challenge due to active conflict, insecurity and bureaucratic impediments, making it difficult for aid organisations to reach those in need. Our programmes primarily include rapid response to emergencies, multipurpose cash assistance, legal protection, education, shelter, and water, sanitation and hygiene. Beyond this, NRC co-leads or supports coordination structures in both countries, including Shelter, CCCM and Protection clusters and the HLP and Durable Solutions Working Groups.

**What you will do:**

The Advocacy Advisor plays a pivotal role in shaping NRC’s policy influence and public positioning in Somalia and Kenya, two of the most complex humanitarian contexts globally. Operating at a senior level, the role leads the design and implementation of advocacy and communications strategies, ensuring coherence with country programme priorities and global standards. It provides expert analysis, develops evidence based advocacy products, and represents NRC in key fora, while also building the capacity of staff and partners to amplify the voices of displaced communities. By bridging operational realities with policy engagement, the Advocacy Advisor ensures NRC’s responses are not only impactful on the ground but also contribute to systemic change at national, regional, and international levels.

General Responsibilities:

1. Identify and coordinate NRC’s advocacy response to prioritised issues both within the country and internationally
2. Develop and implement an impactful advocacy and communications strategy, aligned with the overall country strategy.
3. Develop CO media plan and lines, ensuring risk analyses are made regarding public positions or statements and sign-off procedures are adhered to
4. Line management of communications teams, including development of staff if applicable, budget planning and execution, and other administration
5. Ensure systematic training on advocacy and communication to develop capacity of all relevant staff (within and beyond the advocacy and media department) and ensure compliance with NRC policies, e.g. informed consent, data protection, social media standards

Specific responsibilities:

1. Strategically and ethically raise issues and voices of displaced people in Somalia and Kenya to the attention of decision-makers, duty-bearers, and the public, through both traditional and innovative means
2. Increase accountability of NRC Somalia and Kenya through providing regular and consistent information publicly, about the situations we are responding to and the state of our response (or contributions to coordinated responses)
3. Contribute to Country Office and Area Office problem, protection, and programme analyses and ‘systems thinking’ with a policy lens and a public interest lens, and subsequently promote that relevant policy, advocacy, and communications elements are integrated when designing responses and strategies
4. Coordinate and monitor implementation and impact of NRC Somalia, Kenya, etc. advocacy and media plans and strategies
5. Prepare high quality briefings, reports, press statements, letters, and other communications materials (including visual, digital, and social media) for internal coordination and external use

**Please read the** [**full Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCTQMUUk7ptS4YRhDoAd2svASLS69XHBdPcOta_N73QWUg?e=cMfDfW) **as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

**Generic professional competencies:**

- Post-graduate with minimum five years of relevant experience within the humanitarian field or international media/organisations
- Must have humanitarian advocacy experience and policy management from different contexts.
- Relevant experience in advocacy, communications, media, or humanitarian policy
- Experience working in complex and insecure contexts, preferably in the Horn of Africa
- Strong understanding of humanitarian coordination architecture and donor environments
- Proven experience engaging media and managing sensitive external communications
- Experience producing high-level advocacy products and policy analysis.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- High levels of flexibility and creativity
- Documented professional experience of working in or with international media
- Strong managerial and interpersonal skills
- Fluency in English with strong verbal and written communications skills

**Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Nairobi **(national contract)**
- Contract: 24 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: *70% of dedicated time to the Somalia country office, including regular visits to Somalia (once every 3 months); 10% dedicated time to the Kenya country office; and 20% travel to other countries in East Africa to be identified.*
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **national** salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Applicants should include to their Cover Letter, links to their three most compelling advocacy, media & communications production in their cover letter, ideally one text, one video, one TV/radio interview.**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Kenya. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency permits.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Program Development and Awards Advisor, WACAR
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***The IRC is seeking two (2) Program Development & Award Advisors. These positions are open to candidates in the West and Central Africa Region (WACAR), or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply.***

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD**.** The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**West and Central Africa Regional Overview**

The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR) supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches.

WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The regional team responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the PDAAs oversee a diverse portfolio of awards across the humanitarian, recovery, and development sectors. PDAAs liaise with country programs, HQ departments and donor contacts to ensure high-quality guidance and support to country offices throughout the award lifecycle.

These roles will support country programs in the West and Central Africa region (WACAR) with donor compliance, award management, and producing high-quality donor deliverables. They will advise on IRC’s partnership system (PEERS), manage donor relationships including with HQ counterparts.

In addition, these roles will support WACAR country programs in securing funding for their programmes, through supporting and leading pursuit of new funding opportunities, in line with IRC’s Business Development Strategy. Support includes all phases of the business development process, from opportunity identification to contract signature, including pre-positioning, partnerships building, proposal development, and due diligence phases.

Successful candidates will have a strong track record of contributing to new humanitarian and development funding opportunities, deep knowledge of donor rules and regulations, and experience collaborating with local partner organizations.

**Scope and Authority**

These roles have no line management responsibilities.

**Key Working Relationships**

These positions will report jointly to the Senior Program and Awards Advisor (SPAA) and the Head of Business Development (HBD) for the WACAR region and work closely with RPAS team members, country program grants and partnership teams, and across all teams within the Awards Management Unit, Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, Technical Excellence, and other key departments within IRC. PDAAs also serve as donor and partner points of contact as applicable per region.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

***Awards Management and Compliance***

- Manage a portfolio of awards for the WACAR region as assigned.
- Provide timely support on narrative reporting and post-award deliverables, guiding country offices on amendments, modifications, and submissions while collaborating with technical and financial staff.
- Provide support on budget realignments, changes in scope, NCEs, and other amendments for project elements not captured at proposal stage or emerging needs.
- Serve as first point of contact for country program-based awards staff to problem solve, guide and advise them on compliance post-award issues within the mentioned portfolio and to act as a connecting point between country program and other AMU teams to facilitate the timely flow of key information between them.
- Manage donor relationships by maintaining communication on contractual issues, updates on program implementation and following up on compliance queries and securing changes and approvals as needed.
- With support from the Program & Awards Officer (PAO), guide and coach country offices on partner management policies and PEER system compliance, and review and process sub-grants/partnership agreements. Coordinate with the Sub-awards and Partnerships (S&P) team as needed.
- Provide support to and monitor projects to ensure compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, project implementation meetings and targeted calls following specific donor internal guidelines and IRC established processes.
- In collaboration with other regional team members, monitor award spending and help problem-solve for under-/over-spending. Partner with country programs and regional team as needed, to address implementations challenges.
- Provide technical advice to country offices on ad-hoc queries on donor compliance issues in coordination with AMU’s Compliance and Policy team on non-routine and high-level compliance matters and escalate to leadership for support as needed.
- Take part in meetings and calls with country teams where required to provide support and collaborate closely on specific issues related to donor compliance, submissions and/or monitoring/award management.
- Ensure lessons learned from finalized projects are fed back into new Business Development.
- Advise and support country programs appropriately to enable them to successfully follow internal IRC policies and procedures and maintain the integrity of awards-related data (e.g. OTIS, PEERS).
- Stay informed about programmatic issues and security and political developments affecting implementation.
- Coordinate with other members of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) Team and other AMU members for information sharing and establishing a coherent awards support.
- Ensure proper donor-related and contractual documentation to support compliance and audit readiness (including maintaining up-to-date, organized award files).
- Participate in the recruitment of and the onboarding of new CP Grants Coordinators/Heads of Grants teams.
- Contribute to the development of training materials, and deliver training to in-country staff, as required and in coordination with the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and Program and Award Support (PAS) team leaders. In coordination with the DAM and PAS leaders, develop and maintain work-processes and checklists for award implementation and report review, as well as record lessons learned.
- Onboard new country office Grants and Partnerships staff and new PAS team members to assigned donors, policies and/or IRC processes, as requested.
- Mentor and coach Grants and Partnerships staff on IRC systems and processes to ensure capacity is built at country level.
- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

***Business Development***

- undefined
- Help drive business development in the region by providing effective proposal support, ranging from direct proposal management to light quality assurance.
- Support country offices with donor engagement, intel sharing and positioning with prioritized donors in the PDAA portfolio; prepare for and participate in donor calls as needed.
- Represent IRC externally at country-specific meetings, with donors and stakeholder networks in donor capitals as needed.
- Coordinate proposal development, including sharing initial assessments of new opportunities, preparing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections.
- Collaborate with regional technical leads and technical advisors, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning proposals and designs for new project activities and/or amendments to current projects.
- Provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements, including the PEER system.
- Lead or support coordination, communication, and inputs from consortium partners in accordance with donor and IRC processes.
- Coordinate and support regional reviews and approvals of proposal packages depending on country and regional needs. This includes partners’ packages if applicable.
- Review agreements to ensure accurateness and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with compliance and country grants teams and support in award negotiation and hand-over as required.
- Work with RPAS to incorporate lessons learned from implementation at the proposal stage.
- Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers.

Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:

- \*\*Good understanding of humanitarian aid and development programming
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a diverse team and handle a multifaceted workload
- Good financial management and budgeting skills
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information
- Proven organizational skills, detail-oriented, ability to prioritize tasks, and to learn quickly
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to work independently in a very fast paced environment
- A flexible and calm work attitude
- International work experience in the Global South is a plus
- Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)
- Ability to travel internationally, sometimes on short notice and to insecure areas (15%)

Experience:

- Experience with and a strong understanding of institutional donors’ compliance requirements, e.g. UN, World Bank, US government, and/or European government donors (experience with all is not required, but a good mix would be a strong asset)
- Working at a distance and supporting country-based staff
- Writing, reviewing and editing narrative and financial reports and excellent attention to detail
- Working on new funding opportunities in the humanitarian and international development sectors with a range of multilateral and bilateral donors (FCDO, EU and ECHO, GFFO, BMZ, Sida, SDC, World Bank, US Department of State, etc.), as well as experience collaborating with local partner organizations.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US, UK, EU, German, Scandinavian, etc.

**Compensation (UK):** (GBP 52,210 -GBP 58,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation.
