- Produce written learning resources including blog posts, information guides and toolkits
- Incorporate feedback from internal and external reviewers
- Lead development of multimedia resources, including e-learning modules, videos, and podcasts, in collaboration with colleagues across teams
- Coordinate a monthly community of practice focused on refugee and newcomer emerging topic needs

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

**Required:**

- Master’s Degree in a relevant field, such as Master of Social Work (MSW) or equivalent experience.
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience providing pre- and post-arrival services to newcomer clients, supporting their access to educational, financial, medical, social, and community resources while promoting self-sufficiency

**Preferred:**

- Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Master of Social Work (MSW), or equivalent experience
- Direct service work experience in refugee and newcomer education services
- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
body:
**Background/IRC Summary**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future.

The IRC's Technology department is the engine behind the organization’s ambition to reach 40 million clients by 2033. We are transforming how we work to reach more people through technology and enable faster, better decisions, whilst maintaining a reliable operational foundation that drives down the cost of delivery.

**Job Overview**

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Relationship Management and Engagement**

- Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
- Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
- Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
- Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
- Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
- Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
- Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

**Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance**

- Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
- Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
- Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

title: PALESTINE - HEAD OF LOGISTIC DEPARTMENT - JERUSALEM
body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date:** 1 February 2027  
**Duration of the mission:** 12 months  
**Location:** Jerusalem

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International operates across the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, with operational teams in Deir el-Balah and Ramallah and mission coordination in Jerusalem (although some national coordination staff work out of Ramallah). The position works at coordination level and covers both Gaza and West Bank operations, ensuring consistent administrative, HR and financial support across the mission. SI delivers emergency and early-recovery WASH assistance, shelter and essential-item distributions, and is scaling up nutrition-sensitive FSL activities, including a EUR 1.3 million FIFSAN project with a Palestinian partner. The portfolio relies on close cooperation with local organizations and must continually adapt to volatile access, damaged infrastructure, fragile markets and supply constraints. The Palestinian context is a particularly volatile one, especially in recent months in the West Bank, and in Gaza there are for the moments no signs of a resolution to the political and humanitarian crisis engulfing the exclave and its 2 million residents.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

The Logistic Coordinator steers a mission’s logistical activities in order to ensure that Solidarités International in-country programs run smoothly. He/she implements Solidarités International mission procedures and logistical tools, and ensures that they are properly used and adhered to. He/she participates in defining Solidarités International’s mission strategy, in drawing up projects and in assessing the resources needed for Solidarités International activities. He/she supports the Head of Mission in operational security management. He/she is the point of reference for the mission and serves as the link between headquarters and the mission for all matters relating to logistics.

**The main challenges:**

1\) Shift the department from reactive emergency support to proactive, structured logistics without losing surge capacity.  
2\) Manage simultaneous Gaza, West Bank and Jerusalem timelines, including the heavy 2720 workload, access constraints, fragile markets and international pipelines.  
3\) Improve joint planning and communication between Programs, Access/Liaison and Logistics from proposal design through delivery.  
4\) Understanding the tax and other bureaucratic implications of import from Israel, Jerusalem, and West Bank.

**Security constraints:**

The position is based at coordination level in Jerusalem, with frequent visits to Ramallah. Jerusalem presents no major security constraints, but the wider mission context remains volatile: Gaza faces major security and access challenges, while movement in parts of the West Bank can be restricted and occasionally exposed to violence. All travel to Gaza or outside usual areas is subject to security validation. Strict compliance with movement procedures is required.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Master's degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Engineering, Business Administration or a related field is preferred.

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 yars

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong command of humanitarian supply chain management: procurement, international supply, transport, warehousing, fleet, equipment and premises.
2. Ability to transition from emergency arrangements to standard SI logistics procedures while keeping rapid-response capacity and simplifying processes where appropriate.
3. Experience with market assessments, framework agreements, supplier management, pipeline planning and procurement planning from proposal stage.
4. Strong Excel and logistics reporting skills; confident use of procurement and supply planning tools, including the Procurement Planning Tool.
5. Knowledge of donor compliance, import and customs processes, tax-exemption mechanisms and access-related supply constraints is an asset.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Experience working in Arab culture, and knowledge of how to approch and communicate with national staff
2. Excellent organization and prioritization skills, with the ability to meet multiple deadlines.
3. Ability to model good behavior and team work across a diverse team in a politically, socially, and religious complex context
4. Clear communication and ability to manage frustration in stressful situations
5. Ability to learn, with a strong growth mindset
6. High standards of rigor, integrity, accountability, discretion and confidentiality.
7. Adaptability, initiative and strong cross-department collaboration with Program, Access/Liaison and Coordination teams.

**LANGUAGES**

1. English is mandatory
2. Arabic is not mandatory but highly desirable and may compensate for some experience

## SI WILL OFFER YOU

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

SI has a coordination office in Sheikh Jarrah and an equipped guesthouse in Shuafat with internet, kitchen, laundry and shared living areas. Jerusalem is generally safe and movement in most areas is possible. Staff should avoid walking alone at night and must not visit outskirts, settlements or refugee camps without prior validation. Some neighborhoods can be sensitive. Access to Ramallah is generally manageable but may be affected by checkpoints and temporary movement restrictions.

title: Senior Health Technical Lead/Specialist
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGOs), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities, helping people survive, reclaim control of their futures, and strengthen their communities.

The IRC was present in Sudan from 1981 to 2009. In November 2019, the IRC re-registered in Sudan and, with the wider IRC-led Consortium (CARE International, Catholic Relief Services, Medical Teams International, Relief International, and local partners), currently delivers integrated health and nutrition services across 11 states, supporting 640 health facilities and service delivery points nationwide and reaching over four million beneficiaries in 2025.

Since the outbreak of war in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the country has spiraled into relentless violence, institutional collapse, and mass displacement, and is facing one of the most complex and devastating humanitarian crises in the world today. More than 30 million people now require humanitarian assistance, and around 25 million people face acute food insecurity, including 770,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition.

The project is expected to run for the duration of the World Bank-financed award (exact start date and duration to be confirmed on award).

**Senior Health Technical Lead Scope of Work**

The IRC is seeking a Senior Health Technical Lead for an upcoming World Bank-funded health project in Sudan. The project is intended to restore access to a basic package of health and nutrition services and preserve the main elements of essential public health functions in Sudan.

The project is expected to run from February 2027 for 3 years.

The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical leadership and quality assurance across SHARE II's health and nutrition service delivery and health system strengthening activities including primary health care and hospital services, nutrition programming (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive, maternal and newborn health, disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, health information systems (DHIS2/EWARS/HMIS), and facility-level WASH and infection prevention and control. They will ensure service delivery is technically sound, aligned with national health strategies and World Bank requirements. SHARE II will sustain and maintain SHARE I’s existing footprint in delivering a basic package of health services to 420 PHCs and 10 hospitals and also expand access to essential health services in prioritized high-need localities. The project will be delivered nationwide across multiple states including RSF and SAF controlled areas and many areas with severe to catastrophic health needs.

The postholder will lead facility readiness assessments and IPC protocols; oversees nutrition programming and evidence generation; supports health workforce strengthening, referral pathways, and differentiated delivery models; and provides technical guidance on DHIS2/HMIS, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and emergency response, climate-resilient facility and WASH improvements, laboratory and blood systems, digital health, and supply chain/pharmaceutical management, coordinating closely with Consortium partners.

The Senior Health Technical Lead represents the IRC-led consortium in relevant technical coordination mechanisms (Health, Nutrition and WASH Clusters, Strategic Advisory Group, technical working groups), liaising with WHO, UNICEF, and Federal/State Ministries of Health, and reinforcing government-led systems. They ensure technical activities comply with World Bank Operational Policy 7.30, the Procurement Regulations, and the Environmental and Social Framework, including SEA/SH prevention and response; supports the Third-Party Monitoring mechanism, IRC's Community Feedback Mechanisms and the project's Grievance Redress Mechanism; and supports continuity of SRH and GBV services across the Consortium.

The Senior Health Technical Lead supports the phased, consultative handover of SHARE I sites into SHARE II, ensuring continuity of services, staffing, incentives, commodities and data systems during transition, and contributes to sustainability and responsible exit planning, including integration into MoH plans. The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical inputs to project reporting, including results framework/indicator tracking for submission to the Project Director and the World Bank, and supports capacity building of MoH and local partner staff consistent with IRC's Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS).

**Requirements**

- Medical degree (MD/MBBS) or an advanced degree (Master's) in public health, health systems management, or a related field.
- Minimum 10-15 years' progressive experience in health systems strengthening and/or PHC and hospital service delivery programming, including significant experience in Sudan or comparable fragile, conflict-affected, or access-constrained settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in health and nutrition and relevant technical areas including PHC/hospital service delivery, nutrition (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive/maternal/newborn health, GBV/SRH, mental health, disease surveillance and outbreak response and health information system.
- Prior experience on large health and nutrition projects financed by the World Bank or other major institutional donors; familiarity with health cluster coordination.
- Experience working with, or through, Ministry of Health structures and health-sector coordination mechanisms (Health Cluster, WHO, UNICEF).
- Strong data analysis, facility assessment (HeRAMS), and technical report writing skills, and demonstrated experience supporting multi-partner consortium coordination.
- Fluency in English required; Arabic strongly preferred, given the requirement for field-facing engagement with MoH/SMoH counterparts and communities.
- Ability to travel to field locations across Sudan, including hard-to-reach and access-constrained areas, and to operate effectively under insecure or volatile conditions, in line with IRC and UNDSS security protocols.

Please note that this position will be contingent on the outcome of the bid.

In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. title: Youth Education Specialist (YESOL)
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Background/IRC Summary:**  
The International Rescue Committee responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic well-being, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. The Education and Learning Program provides year-round programming working directly with refugee youth, their parents and families, and their schools.

**Job Overview/Summary:**  
The Youth Education Specialist (YESOL) will work closely with the Youth Programs Supervisor to support high-quality programming for refugee and immigrant youth in New York City. The specialist will be working on a team that works on youth programs including, but not limited to, Youth Tutoring, online Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes, Leaders in Training (LIT), a college access and career readiness program for high school juniors and seniors, World Explorers, a cultural awareness program, and sports programming. During the annual Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA), the Youth Education Specialist will provide logistical support to teaching staff, coordinate instructional coaching, coordinate classroom assessment materials, and collect, enter, and analyze assessment data, ensuring the overall day-to-day classroom needs of the Academy are met. The specialist will also support with instruction and field trips during Mini-NYSA programs, which occur during school breaks in the middle of the school year.

**Major Responsibilities:**

This position will lead Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes:

**Curriculum Preparation**

- Create and improve YESOL curriculum to meet the needs of current student population, including academic English and test preparation
- Prepare slideshows for each class
- Update syllabi for each group as semester progresses

**Intake and Assessment**

- Manage new referral and contact information, outreach to potential families and students
- Administer baseline, midline and endline English assessments, coordinate intake process
- Collaborate with parents and teachers to identify specific student needs

**Teach YESOL Classes**

- 2-3 groups of Middle School: Beginner and Intermediate
- 2 groups of High School: Beginner and Intermediate
- Additional groups based on student need and program capacity

**YESOL Program Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Track class attendance and document daily individual and class case notes
- Gather qualitative data of program impact through student surveys and staff observations
- Synthesize and present data for annual reports

**Intern Management**

- Recruit and hire Youth ESOL interns
- Delegate weekly tasks and review submitted projects and tasks
- Provide opportunities for leadership and professional development

**Saturday Parent ESOL Classes**

- Take lead on managing ESOL classes for parents of youth programs students

**Mini Newcomer Youth Spring Academy (Mini NYSA) and Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA) Support** — direct responsibility for the academic program

- Support NYSA program planning, including staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Plan and instruct lessons on ESOL and other topics to groups of up to 25 students
- Participate in all Meet & Greets, staff trainings, program meetings, and staff development activities thereafter
- Assist the Dean of Instruction in the implementation and analysis of various student assessment initiatives, including but not limited to content area assessments, progress reports, and report cards
- Monitor submission of, enter, and analyze student assessment data
- Assist in the timely production and dissemination of necessary assessments and resources for all teaching staff
- Assist in the coordination and set up of caregiver-teacher conferences
- Assist in the coordination and implementation of school-wide Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS)
- Lead the coordination and implementation of all staff-appreciation events and initiatives
- Lead groups of students for off-site field trips
- Perform other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position reports to: Youth Programs Supervisor
- Position directly supervises: Interns
- Other internal and/or external contacts: Other youth program staff

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree in education or relevant field; Master's degree candidate in education preferred
- Must be available for Saturdays to run programming
- Strong command of Microsoft Suite, G Suite, Canva, and other digital platforms required
- Classroom teaching experience preferred (both in-person and online, especially TESOL experience)
- Experience with data collection and analysis
- Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail
- Strong written and oral communication skills
- Cultural competence and cross-cultural or overseas experience required
- Experience working with immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team

title: Program Officer, Instructional Design & Multimedia
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design and Multimedia for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org.

This position designs and produces the learning experiences newcomers encounter across Settle In’s platforms. The role combines two areas of practice: instructional design—structuring multilingual, self-paced learning journeys that help newcomers build knowledge over time—and multimedia production—creating videos, graphics, and other assets that support the full range of Settle In content.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Design multilingual, self-paced learning journeys for newcomer audiences, including learning objectives, sequencing, knowledge checks, and reinforcement. Apply instructional design, adult learning principles, plain language standards, and translation-ready structure so that content is usable by newcomers with varying levels of literacy, digital literacy, and prior exposure to U.S. systems.
- In partnership with Switchboard’s Senior Program Officer, Instructional Design, establish instructional design standards for Settle In content and review materials developed by team members, subject matter experts, and contractors against those standards.
- Incorporating Switchboard’s established instructional design standards, recommend and implement improvements to Settle In’s instructional design practice, and update previously developed Settle In learning resources on an established review cycle.
- Create compelling, in-language multimedia content, including short-form video, infographics, motion graphics, and social media assets.
- Manage post-production of all finalized work, including Adobe Premiere project organization, color correction and grading, sound design, motion graphics, music editing, sequencing, export and compression for multiple platforms, and archiving.
- Coordinate with the multilingual Digital Community team on content creation, voiceover, subtitling, and translation review, and advise colleagues on audio and video recording tools and practices.
- Ensure final products are easy to understand, culturally appropriate, linguistically and factually accurate, accessible across web and mobile, and aligned with Settle In standards, newcomer needs, and funder requirements.
- Ensure all learning experiences and multimedia content meet accessibility standards (e.g., captions, alt text, screen-reader compatibility)
- Maintain visual and instructional consistency across Settle In's platforms (website, mobile app, social media)
- Coordinate and incorporate feedback across teams and projects and participate in user testing and other methods for optimization of content.
- Manage production timelines across concurrent projects and coordinate the work of external contractors, including videographers, designers, and translation vendors.
- Use platform data and user insights to set measurable goals for content and assess performance, and contribute to project reports, including monthly activity updates and performance monitoring reports.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, communications, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum four years of professional experience combining instructional design and multimedia production, including creating multilingual digital content for diverse populations.
- Demonstrated experience designing self-paced learning for adult audiences, including experience with e-learning tools.
- Excellent command of video editing (Adobe Premiere) and graphic design software (Adobe InDesign, Canva), and knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook.
- Working knowledge of plain language principles and digital accessibility standards.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting).
- Ability to manage complex projects on strict timelines, with excellent written and oral communication skills and strong attention to detail.
- Fluency in at least one of Settle In’s supported languages (Dari, Pashto, Spanish, and Haitian Creole) preferred.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways, and familiarity with ORR-funded programs.
- Ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand learning content
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts, consultants, or production vendors.

title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.

- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.

title: Client Voices Promoter
body:
**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

IRC believes that designing our strategies and programs based on clients’ particular needs and preferences is one of the most critical drivers of impact. We also believe that we have a role to play in working with clients so that they can engage as an equal, influential partner both with IRC and in the broader community through advocacy. The Client Voices Promoters will play a key role in supporting client engagement, and feedback initiatives at the local level. Promoters will work to bring together multi-ethnic, multi-racial and multi-sector constituencies to build the power of refugees and immigrants and the organizations that serve them to ensure their sustainability and improve people’s lives.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Partner with IRC program staff to execute client satisfaction and feedback initiatives, including surveys and focus group discussions.
- Collaborate with clients to ensure their feedback informs IRC program planning and service improvements.
- Identify and implement preferred client engagement and feedback methods tailored to community needs.
- Act as a liaison between IRC and local refugee communities, representing their concerns and suggestions to office leadership.
- Support client participation in discussions with external partners to amplify their influence on broader community strategies.
- Attend community events and workshops to maintain strong connections with refugee communities and identify areas for program enhancement.
- Organize and facilitate leadership and civic engagement training sessions to empower clients as advocates and community leaders.
- Coordinate community events and focus groups to encourage active client involvement in IRC decision-making processes.
- Ensure alignment with IRC’s client complaints and feedback policies, supporting consistent and ethical practices.
- Maintain accurate records of feedback and engagement initiatives to track progress and inform future strategies.
- Proactively engage with clients and raise their issues to IRC leadership to inform organizational priorities.
- Perform additional tasks as assigned to support IRC’s mission and client-centered programming.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Undergraduate degree preferred, in relevant field of study.
- Minimum 3 years of work experience.
- Demonstrated experience working with refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, and/or immigrant populations required.
- Community outreach experience preferred.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively and build relationships with colleagues and partners in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment, and the ability to present to a varied public required.
- Solid organizational skills with the ability to juggle multiple tasks, set priorities, effectively manage time, and meet deadlines required.
- Fluency in English, both verbal and written, is required. Fluency in other languages and cultures of the local refugee population including Arabic, Swahili, French and Pashto/Dari is strongly preferred.
- A valid driver’s license, reliable vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area required.

title: Clinical Services Supervisor
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, inclusive and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Clinical Services Supervisor oversees and provides culturally, and linguistically appropriate mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) designed to improve the holistic well-being of human trafficking survivors. The position has four main functions: 1) Clinical services - conducting mental health intakes and assessments, developing individual service plans, and delivering evidence-based and evidence-informed interventions, 2) Clinical supervision - supervising non-licensed psychosocial support staff to ensure services are of quality, trauma informed, and culturally relevant, and 3) Care coordination - with internal and external providers to ensure holistic client support, and 4) Outreach and engagement - to build provider and community capacity to identify, respond to, and serve survivors of human trafficking. The Clinical Services Supervisor must be an independently licensed counselor/therapist in WA State. Strong candidates must have experience helping help high barriers clients navigate and access systems, and delivering culturally responsive, linguistically accessible services. This position reports to the MHPSS Program Manager with clinical supervision provided by IRC’s MHPSS Technical Advisor.

**Clinical Responsibilities:**

- Supervision
- Ensure clinical quality of programming
- Conduct intake and assessment and develop individual service plans
- Provide interventions and activities in-office, remotely, and in community settings
- Maintain a clinical case load (approx. 15-20 clients)
- Manage crisis (i.e., suicide assessments, safety planning, mandatory reporting, etc.)
- Care coordination including warm hand-offs as needed
- Support development and delivery of psychoeducation training to IRC staff and community partners to strengthen response and services for survivors of human trafficking.
- Supervise master’s level Practicum Interns

**Project Management Responsibilities:**

- Arrange for interpreters as needed to appropriately engage clients in services
- Ensure timely and accurate documentation, data entry, and reporting
- Monitor program activity and quality through oversight and support related to case and project documentation
- Evaluate effectiveness of program related to client progress and individual service plan objectives
- Communicate and coordinate regularly with all levels of program staff to ensure that services are being delivered effectively and in a timely manner
- Strengthen and maintain partnerships with community mental health agencies to expand client resources
- Deliver capacity-building initiatives to strengthen community response and services for human trafficking victims
- Other duties as assigned

***External*****:** *API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.*

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Holds a valid Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW) in the state of Washington

- At least two years’ experience providing evidence-based, evidence-informed, or best-practice interventions
- At least one year of supervisor experience
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Strong intercultural communication skills: demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds
- Strong computer, keyboard, email, and general office skills

title: PIR Case Management Specialist
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Case Management Specialist provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. This position splits time between two programs: approximately 70% in ORR's Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and approximately 30% in the Home ARP program. The Case Management Specialist works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide case management services across two funding streams, dedicating approximately 70% of time to PIR clients and 30% to Home ARP clients, ensuring program requirements and documentation standards are met for each.
- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Help clients find and apply for permanent housing and support them through the move-in process.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days, up to 90 days of service.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information into IRC’s case documentation database, ETO, and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Case Management Coordinator

**Indirect Reporting:** Economic Wellbeing Manager and Senior Health and Wellness Program Manager

WARN Mental Health Advocate
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Mental Health Advocate supports the mental health and resilience of survivors of trafficking through the WARN program, providing one-on-one peer support, referrals, and group-based services. This client-facing role includes one on one support, offering psychoeducation and skill-building workshops, and facilitating MHPSS groups. The Mental Health Advocate also coordinates program logistics, recruit participants, documents services, and supports evaluation through data collection. Additionally, they connect clients to appropriate mental health resources, assist with care coordination, and collaborate with supervisors to provide crisis support as needed.

- Recruit and enroll participants for WARN programs.
- Plan and organize logistics for WARN programs, including scheduling, transportation, materials, and space coordination.

**Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Document client interactions and program activities through detailed case notes and data entry.
- Assist in evaluating current services and identifying opportunities for new program offerings.
- Use IRC software to document client information and other program materials.

**Administrative & Team Support**

- Attend and actively participate in team meetings, staff meetings, and relevant IRC trainings and conference calls.
- Collaborate with supervisor and team members to ensure program quality and compliance.
- Perform other duties as assigned to support the success of WARN programming.

title: Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer, POWER Partnership
body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee helps people affected by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and regain control of their future. The Violence Prevention and Response Unit leads IRC's work across women's protection and empowerment, child protection, and protection and rule of law, positioning social work in crises as the connective practice across these areas.

POWER is a multi-country strategic partnership funded by Irish Aid, running from 2025 to 2027 across Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan. Its core logic is holistic gender-based violence prevention and response delivered through strengthened local women-led organizations, including partners such as SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, with a quarter of country budgets channeled directly to local partners under a feminist partnership framework and the PEERS power-sharing principles. The program includes a dedicated advocacy pillar, an emergency response pillar, and a partnership learning pillar, and it works through practices such as women-led safety audits that already constitute community-generated risk analysis feeding into local advocacy and decision-making.

**Job overview**

The Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer coordinates quality and learning across the six POWER country programs. The role works through country WPE and program teams, POWER’s women-led and local partners, and the WPE Global Practice, and coordinates with the Award Management Unit (AMU), which leads the donor relationship with Irish Aid. It is accountable for technical quality assistance against IRC core WPE standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards for the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, and for tracking and reporting delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six countries so that deviation is identified early. The position contributes to the partnership’s advocacy pillar and to the design of the next partnership phase.

**Major responsibilities**

The role holds the technical quality of POWER delivery to IRC's WPE standards, keeps the partnership and the WPE Global Practice in two-way exchange ,rather than a one directional flow of standards downward, and tracks delivery across six countries against scope, timeline and budget so that deviation is flagged early enough for adaptive management

- Provide quality oversight across the six country programs, so that survivor-centered response, case management, women and girls' safe spaces, clinical and MHPSS referral pathways, and social norms work meet IRC WPE technical standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Serve as the connective role between the POWER partnership and the WPE Global Practice, translating core standards into partnership contexts and carrying partnership-generated practice back into the core.
- Support the sequencing of prevention and social norms activities to context, so they are introduced only where women-led community analysis confirms the preconditions for safe implementation are met.
- Maintain coherence of approach across the six countries without flattening contextual difference, identifying where a shared standard applies and where local adaptation is warranted.
- Track and report on delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six country programs, flagging deviation early enough for adaptive management rather than end-of-cycle correction.
- Ensure MEAL and program data feed directly into program adaptation, so that what the data shows changes what the program does, not only what it reports.
- Connect program data and implementation evidence to wider sector trends and debates, including comparable protection and GBV programming elsewhere.

**Learning, evidence, and the partnership learning agenda**

The role leads the program's learning function, treating implementation learning as a legitimate evidence pathway rather than a lesser substitute for external research. It also support the partnership’s advocacy pillar, so that evidence generated with the partners informs partners’ own advocacy and IRC’s policy positioning.

- Lead the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, coordinating cross-country learning cycles, documentation, and structured reflection between IRC and partners.
- Position women-led safety audits as community-generated risk analysis, and strengthen the pathway from that analysis into local decision-making and adaptive management.
- Build the program's evidence base on what enables and constrains change in protracted crisis settings, surfacing failure modes honestly, including referral systems that exist on paper but not in practice, and norms work that shifts survey scores without shifting community behavior.
- Ensure learning is co-owned with partners and feeds their own institutional positioning, not only IRC's reporting obligations.
- Steward the POWER advocacy pillar, supporting partners to carry community-generated analysis into local, national, and global advocacy where they hold standing in their own right.
- Work with advocacy and policy colleagues so the partnership's evidence informs IRC positioning toward donors, multilaterals, and normative bodies.

**Strengthening the core and surge capacity of women-led and local organizations**

The role supports partners on two distinct fronts, their institutional core and their capacity to surge in emergencies, resisting the pattern where localization language coexists with authority still held by the international actor.

- Support partner institutional strengthening across governance, financial systems, safeguarding, and MEAL in ways partners define and lead, consistent with the PEERS principles and the direct funding commitment.
- Strengthen partner surge and emergency response readiness under the emergency response pillar, so local organizations hold a credible role when crises escalate rather than being displaced by international surge.
- Advance the shift of analytical and decision-making authority toward partners with genuine institutional standing, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, co-designing tools and thresholds with them rather than imposing them.
- Support the broader civil society and women's movement ecosystem the partnership connects to, recognizing partners as governance and coordination actors in their own right.

**Strategic focus on women and girls in conflict settings**

The role keeps women and girls in active conflict and protracted displacement at the center of the partnership, including where conflict-related sexual violence is a feature of the context.

- Ensure program design and adaptation are anchored in the realities faced by women and girls across the six contexts, several of which are shaped by active conflict and large-scale displacement.
- Support conflict-related sexual violence sensitive practice where relevant, including safe and consent-based documentation, clinical pathways, and Do No Harm decisions taken at closest proximity to violence, with pattern awareness fed upward.
- Keep adolescent girls visible as a distinct group rather than folded into a general women-and-girls category.

**Partnership and donor relationship management**

The role supports coherence of technical delivery across countries and reporting cycles, contributing technical content into the strategic relationship with Irish Aid, which AMU stewards and holds overall.

- Serve as a central program coordination point for the POWER partnership, supporting planning, adaptive management, amendments, and quality reporting to Irish Aid in coordination with the European DE & Frameworks team (Irish Aid).
- Feed technical content on program direction, learning, and strategic opportunities into AMU's communication with Irish Aid and the Department of Foreign Affairs. .
- Coordinate across the six country teams and the relevant IRC technical, advocacy, awards, and finance functions to keep the partnership coherent and its commitments met.
- Contribute technical input to AMU's design and negotiation of the next Strategic Partnership phase (post-2027), including program scope, theory of change, and the monitoring, evaluation and learning framework, coordinating input from WPE pillar leads, country teams, and partners, under AMU's overall lead on negotiation, timeline, and the donor relationship.

**Key working relationships**

**Works closely with:** AMU, Global and VPRU Advocacy; VPRU MEAL/METAL Unit.

Country WPE and program leads across the six POWER countries; POWER women-led and local partners, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya; IRC Awards Management Unit (AMU); VPRU Business Development; Irish Aid and Department of Foreign Affairs counterparts.

**Job requirements**

**Education:** Advanced degree in a relevant field such as social work, gender studies, international development, human rights, public health, or law, or an equivalent combination of qualification and experience.

**Work experience:** A minimum of 8 years professional experience in GBV, WPE, or protection programming in humanitarian and conflict-affected settings, at a technical lead level, including demonstrated experience in partnership and locally-led social action, in program quality or learning, and in program or grant management including budget oversight.

**Demonstrated skills and competencies:**

- Strong technical grounding in WPE practice and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Practical experience in feminist partnership and localization, including working with women-led organizations as partners rather than subgrantees.
- Learning and MEAL capability, with the judgment to treat implementation learning as evidence and to surface difficult findings.
- Program and grant management across multiple countries, including tracking and reporting r delivery against scope, timeline, and budget, and the systems to flag deviation early.
- Ability to translate program evidence into policy-relevant framing for donors, multilaterals, and normative processes.
- Multi-country coordination across diverse and often insecure contexts, with contextual and political sensitivity.
- Sound Do No Harm and safeguarding judgment, particularly in conflict-related sexual violence contexts.

**Languages:** Fluent English required. French is an asset given the East and Central Africa footprint, and Arabic is an asset for the Sudan and South Sudan contexts.

**Working environment and travel:** Possible travel across the six countries, including to hardship and conflict-affected locations.

***This is a hybrid position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Uganda, Burundi.***

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:** The Employment Supervisor is responsible for leading a team that provides employment services including assessment, self-sufficiency planning, job readiness training, vocational/skills training, job search, job placement, post-placement support and employer partnership development and maintenance. The supervisor focuses on attaining grant deliverables, most frequently surrounding job training, placement, wage and retention. This position supervises a team, monitors data, ensures program goals are met and supports quality control to support both service provision and contractual compliance.

**Responsibilities: Include, but are not limited to:**

**Staff Management:**

- Lead and develop direct service staff through facilitation of team meetings and individual supervision including coaching and goal setting.
- Assign cases, oversee staff workload, help prioritize, troubleshoot and generally support.
- Ensure compliance with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency.
- Maintain communication with staff regarding challenging cases; carry out timely and professional interventions to ensure quality service delivery and to achieve desired results.

**Client Services:**

- Supervise program implementation including assessment, self-sufficiency planning, job readiness training, job search, job placement, post-placement support and employer partnership development and maintenance. Maintain consistent focus on grant deliverables
- Coordinate training activities, ensuring high quality services that meet funder requirements. This may include internal and external job readiness, skill development and/or vocational trainings.
- Track enrolled clients using assigned database system(s) to ensure services are provided in a timely manner and properly documented.
- Develop and maintain relationships with local employers, ensuring consistent job placement opportunities for clients.
- Develop strategic partnerships with community organizations, focused on advancing program objectives and client success.

**Program Oversight:**

- Coordinate quality assurance efforts by conducting periodic case file and database reviews.
- Monitor the employment team's progress toward grant deliverables, develop systems to share progress and support improvements with an eye toward fulfilling funder and agency requirements. Propose interventions when programs are not on point to meet deliverables.
- Monitor direct assistance spending to ensure timely and appropriate use of funds.
- Coordinate across teams and departments to support overall client wellbeing.

**Job Requirements:**

- University degree required, preferably in International Studies, Business, Social Services or a related field OR equivalent work experience.

- Experience supervising, supporting, and training staff.
- Proven success in promoting an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a variety of skills and perspectives.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
- Maintain accurate case notes and data entry in required systems; prepare employment vouchers and other documentation.
